module_title: MS Access - Advanced Data Types, OLE Objects, and Referential Integrity
introduction: Tailored for SSC CGL Tier-2 (Mains) and technical banking exams, this advanced module analyzes the strict 'Data Types' assigned during table creation, multimedia embedding (OLE), and advanced database security rules.

core_concepts.title: Crucial Data Types
core_concepts.description:
- Short Text: Used for standard text and numbers (like Names or Cities). It has a strict maximum limit of exactly 255 characters.
- Long Text (formerly Memo): Used for heavy paragraphs (like Remarks or Feedback). It can hold up to 64,000+ characters.
- AutoNumber: A unique Access data type that automatically generates a sequential number (1, 2, 3...) for every new record created. It is most commonly used to automatically generate Primary Keys.

core_concepts.title: OLE Object (Object Linking and Embedding)
core_concepts.description: If you need to attach a heavy external file to a database record—such as a photograph, an MS Word document, or an Excel chart—you must set the field's data type to 'OLE Object'.

core_concepts.title: Validation Rule
core_concepts.description:
A logical condition set by the database administrator to prevent wrong data entry. 
Example: If you set a Validation Rule of `>=18` on the 'Age' column, the system will throw an error and completely reject the entry if a user tries to type '15'.

core_concepts.title: Referential Integrity
core_concepts.description: An advanced security rule applied between two linked tables. It ensures that you cannot accidentally delete a master record if it is actively being used in another table (e.g., you cannot delete a Customer's profile if they still have a pending Order linked to their name).

important_entities.name: Yes/No Data Type
important_entities.significance: Used strictly for fields that can only have one of two possible answers (True/False, On/Off, Yes/No). Visually, it usually appears as a clickable checkbox.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A common Tier-2 true/false statement: 'A user can manually edit the value of an AutoNumber field.' The answer is strictly FALSE. AutoNumber is entirely controlled by the MS Access system to guarantee uniqueness; users cannot type into it.
Examiners frequently test the exact physical limit of the 'Short Text' data type. Memorize the number: it is exactly 255 characters. Anything beyond that requires the 'Long Text' data type.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Whenever a question mentions 'photographs', 'graphs', or 'external files' being saved into Access, immediately look for OLE.

exam_strategy_tips: For Mains, remember the invisible connection to SQL (Structured Query Language). Even though MS Access uses a graphical interface to build Queries, it is actually writing and executing SQL code in the background to fetch your data.
